events.title: The Great Persecution begins
events.shortBlurb: At Nicomedia the edicts of Diocletian opened the last and fiercest persecution of the early Church…
body: In February of 303, at his capital of Nicomedia, the Emperor Diocletian unleashed what would be the last and most terrible persecution of the Roman Church. On the twenty-third of February the great cathedral of the city was demolished, and the next day the first edict was published, ordering churches razed to the ground, the sacred Scriptures burned, and Christians stripped of rank and office.

Further edicts soon commanded the clergy imprisoned and all Christians to sacrifice to the gods on pain of death, and for years the faithful suffered across the empire, above all in the East. The storm passed only with the rise of Constantine and the Edict of Milan in 313, which at last granted the Church peace; the memory of its many martyrs the Church has never forgotten.

sources.text: Eusebius, Church History (Book VIII; public-domain translation)
